record.original_question: Extend Chaitin complexity from finite strings to infinite strings. The source proposes two routes: using non-terminating programs that run forever and generate infinite strings in infinite time, or using computational models that handle infinite strings in finite time, such as cellular automata or functions on the reals.

evidence.quote: Chaitin complexity has been defined for finite strings. It would be interesting to extend it to infinite strings. Two ways can be envisaged: – (a) using non-terminating programs, looping forever, and generating infinite strings in an infinite amount of time; – (b) using computational models dealing with infinite strings in finite amounts of time (cellular automata, functions on reals, etc.). (F. Geurts) The first part has already received a small attention. The second one is probably another way to think about this complexity. (F. Geurts)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. For a finite binary string x, the prefix-free Chaitin (Kolmogorov) complexity H(x) is defined as the length of a shortest binary program p such that a fixed universal prefix-free Turing machine U, on input p, halts and outputs x; this quantity depends on U only up to an additive constant.

Problem. Develop a satisfactory extension of Chaitin complexity from finite binary strings to infinite binary sequences ω ∈ {0,1}^ℕ. Specifically, propose and justify a definition of a complexity function H_∞(ω) (or, more generally, an invariant assigning algorithmic-information content to infinite sequences) via one of the following two paradigms, and establish its basic properties (machine-invariance up to additive constants, behavior under computable transformations, relationship to randomness notions for infinite sequences, and analogues of the fundamental theorems known for finite strings, such as the coding theorem and the incompressibility/randomness characterization):

(a) Non-terminating computations. Use programs for a universal machine that need not halt, but that produce, in the limit, an infinite output sequence; define H_∞(ω) in terms of the lengths of such programs that generate ω in infinite time.

(b) Infinite-time computational models. Use models of computation that handle infinite inputs/outputs in finite time, such as cellular automata operating on bi-infinite configurations, computable functions on the real numbers (in the sense of computable analysis), infinite-time Turing machines, or analogous models; define H_∞(ω) as the minimal description length within such a model.

In each case, determine whether the resulting notion is well-defined and machine-independent up to a constant, how it relates to the prefix-free complexity K(ω↾n) of initial segments and to Martin-Löf randomness, and to what extent the classical theory of algorithmic information transfers to the infinite setting.
artifact.status_search_result: Definitions of algorithmic complexity for infinite sequences via initial-segment prefix-free complexity K(ω↾n) are well established and underlie Martin-Löf randomness and related notions (Schnorr, Levin, Chaitin); these correspond to a partial answer to route (a). Complexity notions based on infinite-time Turing machines, computable analysis, and cellular automata have been studied (e.g., Hamkins–Lewis infinite-time Turing machines, Carl, Schindler, and others), but a unified, fully satisfactory Chaitin-style complexity theory for infinite strings encompassing both routes remains incompletely developed. The problem is therefore best described as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Kolmogorov complexity - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The definition of Kolmogorov complexity for random strings can be extended to define a notion of randomness for infinite sequences... an infinite sequence is random if the prefix-free Kolmogorov complexity of its initial segments grows quickly enough.
status_evidence.claim: Route (a)-type extensions via initial-segment complexity are standard and yield Martin-Löf randomness.

status_evidence.title: Algorithmic information theory - Scholarpedia
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithmic information theory principally studies complexity measures on strings (or other data structures)... extensions to infinite sequences underlie definitions of algorithmic randomness.
status_evidence.claim: Algorithmic information theory has developed complexity notions applicable to infinite sequences.
